stem: Find out standard enthalpy of formation of CH 3 OH(l) from following data. CH 3 OH(l) + (3/2)O 2 (g) → CO 2 (g) + 2H 2 O(l); ΔH° = −726 kJ/mole C(graphite) + O 2 → CO 2 (g); ΔH° = −393 kJ/mole H 2 (g) + (1/2)O 2 (g) → H 2 O(l); ΔH° = −286 kJ/mole (A) −239 kJ/mole (B) 239 kJ/mole (C) 47 kJ/mole (D) −47 kJ/mole

The lattice energy of solid NaCl is 180 kcal/mol. The dissolution of the solid in water in the form of ions is endothermic to the extent of 1 kcal/mol. If the hydration energies of Na + and Cl − are in the ratio 6 : 5, what is the enthalpy of hydration of Na + ion? (A) −85.6 kcal mol −1 (B) −97.64 kcal mol −1 (C) +82.6 kcal mol −1 (D) +100 kcal mol −1

Enthalpy of neutralization of H 3 PO 3 (dibasic acid) is −105 kJ/mol using KOH. Enthalpy of neutralization of HCl by KOH is −56 kJ/mol. Calculate ΔH ionization of H 3 PO 3 into its ions: (A) 7 kJ/mol (B) 5 kJ/mol (C) 2.5 kJ/mol (D) 3.5 kJ/mol

The enthalpy of hydrogenation of C₆H₆(l) is −205 kJ and resonance energy of C₆H₆(l) is −152 kJ/mole, then enthalpy of hydrogenation of [cyclohexene, structure shown] is [Given ΔHvap of C₆H₁₀(l), C₆H₆(l), C₆H₁₂(l) all are equal] (a) −519 kJ/mole (b) −229 kJ/mole (c) −619 kJ/mole (d) −119 kJ/mole

Match the List-I with List-II List-I (Thermodynamic Process) a. Work done in reversible, isothermal expansion of 2 mol of gas from 2 dm3 to 20 dm3 at 300 K b. Work done in irreversible isothermal expansion of 1 mol ideal gas from 1 m3 to 3 m3 at 300 K against a constant pressure of 3 kPa c. Change in internal energy for adiabatic expansion of a 1 mol ideal gas with change of temperature = 320 K and Cv = (3/2)R d. Change in enthalpy at constant pressure of 1 mol ideal gas with change of temperature = 337 K and Cp = (5/2)R List-II (Magnitude in kJ) I. 4 II. 11.5 III. 6 IV. 7 (A) a—II, b—I, c—III, d—IV (B) a—I, b—II, c—III, d—IV (C) a—II, b—III, c—I, d—IV (D) a—III, b—II, c—IV, d—I
book_key: C a—II, b—III, c—I, d—IV You marked: A

stem: The heat change for the following reaction at 298 K and constant pressure is +7.3 kcal. A 2 B(s) → 2A(s) + (1/2)B 2 (g); ΔH = +7.3 kcal The heat change at constant volume would be (A) +7.3 kcal (B) more than 7.3 kcal (C) less than 7.3 kcal (D) zero
book_key: C less than 7.3 kcal You marked: B

stem: Which of the following thermodynamic properties must be associated with a reaction found to be spontaneous at high temperatures but not spontaneous at low temperatures? (A) ΔH < 0, ΔS < 0 (B) ΔH < 0, ΔS > 0 (C) ΔH > 0, ΔS > 0 (D) ΔH > 0, ΔS < 0
book_key: C ΔH > 0, ΔS > 0 You marked: B

stem: 16 g oxygen gas expands at STP (against a constant external pressure of 1 atm) to occupy double of its original volume. The work done during the process is : (a) 260 cal (b) 180 cal (c) 130 cal (d) 272.84 cal

The change in entropy of 2 moles of an ideal gas upon isothermal expansion at 243.6 K from 20 L to the state where pressure becomes 1 atm is : (Given : ln 2 = 0.693, R = 0.082 lit atm mole −1 K −1 , R = 2 cal mole −1 K −1 ) (A) 1.385 cal/K (B) −1.2 cal/K (C) 1.2 cal/K (D) 2.77 cal/K

The reversible expansion of an ideal gas under adiabatic and isothermal conditions is shown in the figure (w = work done by the gas). Which of the following statement(s) is (are) correct ? (a) T₁ = T₂ (b) ΔS_isothermal > ΔS_adiabatic (c) w_isothermal > w_adiabatic (d) All of these
book_key: D All of these You marked: C

stem: A coffee cup calorimeter initially contains 125 g of water, at a temperature of 24.2 °C. 8 g of ammonium nitrate (NH 4 NO 3 ), also at 24.2 °C, is added to the water, and the final temperature is 18.2 °C.
